Apple diseases and pests: identification and control

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

Apple tree deaths come mainly from white root rot, collar rot and canker dieback; leaf diseases such as apple scab, Marssonina blotch and Alternaria strip leaves and spoil fruit. Leaf diseases are controlled by leaf sanitation (including the October 5% urea spray) and rotating fungicides from different groups; root diseases by drainage, collar surgery and copper paste. Calendar spraying wastes money and kills the predatory mites that keep red mite in check (SKUAST-K 2026, ICAR-CITH).

Schedule

Apple spray schedule

What to spray at each stage, and when not to spray at all.

Apple scab

Olive velvety spots to dark corky scabs on leaves and fruit.

Powdery mildew

White floury shoot tips; winter pruning and sulphur.

Woolly apple aphid

White wool on twigs and galls on roots.

Apple diseases at a glance

DiseaseSymptomsCurable?Management
White root rotSparse small leaves, collapse; white cottony fungus on brown roots (Jun–Sep)Early onlyDrainage, root exposure, copper paste, drench
Collar rotSlimy red-brown bark rot at the soil line (worst on MM.106 in clay)Early onlyRaised beds, graft 15–20 cm high, Bordeaux paste, drench
Canker and diebackCracked, sunken bark; branches dying from pruning stubsPrune and preventCut 15 cm into healthy wood, sterilise tools, copper paste, whitewash
Apple scabVelvety olive spots turning into dark corky scabs on leaves and fruitPreventiveOctober 5% urea, rotated fungicides
Marssonina blotch and AlternariaPurple-brown blotches turning bright yellow, leaf fall in July–August; frog-eye spots (Alternaria)PreventiveOpen canopy, leaf sanitation, rotated fungicides
Powdery mildewWhite floury shoot tipsManageableWinter pruning of white tips, wettable sulphur
Viruses; fire blightMosaic patches; black shepherd's-crook shoots (fire blight)NoVirus-free planting material; report suspected fire blight to SKUAST or ICAR-CITH

Apple pests at a glance

PestSignsWhenNon-chemical controlRegistered chemicals (as per label)
San Jose scaleAsh-grey crust on bark; red halos on fruitDormant season and summer crawlersPrune encrusted twigs; parasitoid Encarsia perniciosiHorticultural mineral oil 2% at delayed dormant (14–21 days apart from sulphur); summer insecticide as per schedule
European red miteSilvery-bronze leaves, summer leaf drop (check with a 10× lens for red eggs)May–AugustStop calendar pyrethroid sprays that kill predatory mites; dormant oilRotate acaricide groups: hexythiazox, fenazaquin, spiromesifen, propargite
Woolly apple aphidWhite wool on twigs; galls on rootsSpring–autumnResistant MM.106 / MM.111; parasitoid Aphelinus maliImidacloprid or thiamethoxam; root treatment as per schedule
Stem and shot-hole borersCoarse sawdust (stem borer); pinhead holes on stressed trunksSummerFix drought, canker and sunscald first; hooked wire in tunnelsInsecticide plug in tunnels as per label. Dichlorvos, phorate and monocrotophos are banned or withdrawn.
Blossom thripsBrowned, distorted petalsTight cluster to pink budSticky trapsPre-bloom only; never during bloom
Codling mothWorm tunnel to the coreQuarantine pest found only in Ladakh (Leh, Kargil)Strict crate quarantine, pheromone traps, TrichogrammaLadakh IPM schedule (SKUAST-K)

Pesticide safety: Use only pesticides registered for apple by CIB&RC, at the dose and waiting period on the label, and follow your state's current spray schedule (SKUAST-K, Dr. YSP UHF or the state horticulture department). Dichlorvos, monocrotophos, phorate, carbofuran, benomyl and carbaryl are banned, withdrawn or restricted in India.

Questions farmers ask

What are the main diseases of apple in India?

White root rot, collar rot, canker and dieback, apple scab, Marssonina blotch, Alternaria leaf spot and powdery mildew.

Why are apple leaves falling in July–August?

Most often Marssonina blotch or Alternaria, sometimes European red mite. Leaf sanitation, an open canopy and rotated fungicides help.

How do I control red mite in apple?

Stop calendar pyrethroid sprays that kill predatory mites, use dormant oil, and rotate acaricide groups only when counts exceed 5–10 mites per leaf.
